judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are exact, and the second one I checked in the source rather than by eye. Verification coverage: problem 3(a) 'Explain how you can tell Jae's answer is impossible before checking any arithmetic' and 3(b) 'Name the substitution mistake'; problem 5(a) 'Explain why 40 cannot be the hypotenuse here'; problem 6(a) 'Name Kim's mistake --- which segment really is the hypotenuse?'; problem 7(b) 'Which solution is the screen's width, and why must the other one be thrown out?'; and problem 4 'Sketch the right triangle whose hypotenuse is $\overline{AB}$'. verify.json holds eight entries, not one of type manual, and machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags false -- so a required drawn construction and four required diagnoses are all inside the machine-verified count. Missing sketch: answer_key.tex contains zero tikz environments (grep count 0) and never inputs figure-macros, which the worksheet does input; the key's problem 4 only describes the construction in prose -- 'Drop a horizontal and a vertical segment from A and B to build a right triangle' -- so the model response for a drawing task is not drawn. That is the judge's claim verbatim and it holds. All eight values recompute: 10, 12, 15, 13, 41, 10, x = ±56, and 140 - 100 = 40, as do the four declared traps (14, 13.93, 18.79, 10.91, 38.97, 5.29, 87.08).

strengths_to_preserve: The declared trap on every find-the-mistake problem is the exact number the character prints in the stem: Jae's 18.79 is id 3's trap sqrt(17**2 + 8**2); Sam's 38.97 is id 5's trap sqrt(40**2 - 9**2); Kim's 5.29 is id 6's trap sqrt(8**2 - 6**2). The misconception the student is shown and the value the checker proves distinguishable are the same object.

Every solution in the key closes with a size sanity-check tied to the theorem's structure rather than to the arithmetic -- '12 cm, which is shorter than the 13 cm hypotenuse -- the check a leg must pass', and for problem 5 '41 cm, just longer than the 40 cm leg, as expected'. The directions teach the same habit before problem 1 ('a leg must come out shorter than the hypotenuse'), so the sheet, the key and the traps all run on one idea.

Problem 3(a) asks the student to reject Jae's answer BEFORE any arithmetic -- 18.79 feet of wall reached by a 17-foot ladder is impossible on its face. Putting the plausibility judgement ahead of the computation is the single most transferable move on the sheet, and the key answers it in those terms.

Problem 7 is a genuine domain-restriction item rather than a decorated quadratic: $x^2 + 33^2 = 65^2$ has both 56 and -56 as real solutions, and the sheet asks explicitly for 'every value of $x$' before asking which one is the width. The 65-33-56 triple is chosen so the arithmetic is exact and the discarded root is the only difficulty.

root_causes.description: Four required diagnoses and one required drawing are recorded as machine-verified because the coverage rule is satisfied by the numeric half of the same problem. SKILL.md line 257 explicitly lists 'graph sketches ... constructions, and any explanation/reasoning answer' as manual, and line 249 separately says error-analysis can go 'via the ordinary types' -- the second sentence is the one that got applied to a sheet whose entire instructional mode is error analysis, and nothing in the gate chain contradicted it.
evidence: worksheet.tex problems 3, 5 and 6 each print an (a) part that is a pure diagnosis and a (b) part that is the corrected value; verify.json ids 3, 5 and 6 hold one approx/distance entry each
worksheet.tex problem 4: 'Sketch the right triangle whose hypotenuse is $\overline{AB}$' -- verify.json id 4 is a single distance check
verify.json contains no entry with "type": "manual"; machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false
SKILL.md line 257: 'Use `manual` for: graph sketches, sign charts, word problem setups, two-column proofs, constructions, ... and any explanation/reasoning answer.'
SKILL.md line 249: '...and **error-analysis** ("find and fix the mistake") via the ordinary types'

root_causes.description: Problem 7's candidate-selection condition is not verified and the rejected root leaks into the answer key's grading column. verify.json id 7 is a solve with expected [56, -56], which is correct as a solution set, but nothing records that the width is 56 and that -56 is discarded because a length cannot be negative. The Quick Answers bank consequently prints '7. 56, -56' -- a grader reading only the bank sees both roots offered as the answer.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7(b): 'Which solution is the screen's width, and why must the other one be thrown out?'

answer_key.pdf problem 7(b) does state the resolution -- 'a width is a length, and lengths are never negative, so x = -56 is discarded' -- so the reasoning exists in the key but in no check and not in the bank

root_causes.description: The answer key has no mechanism for supplying a figure that the worksheet asks the student to draw. worksheet.tex inputs figure-macros and uses \refrt for its reference right triangle; answer_key.tex inputs neither and contains no tikz at all, so problem 4's model response is a prose description of a drawing. Nothing in the gate chain notices that a problem whose stem says 'Sketch' has a figure-free solution.
evidence: answer_key.tex: no \input{figure-macros}, and grep for 'tikz' returns 0 matches
answer_key.pdf problem 4 solution text: 'Drop a horizontal and a vertical segment from A and B to build a right triangle. Those two are the legs; AB is the hypotenuse'
gate_log.txt: render-figures and compile-ak both PASS

improvements.title: Four error diagnoses and one required sketch are recorded as machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add a manual entry beside the numeric entry for ids 3, 5, 6 and 7 (descs naming the expected diagnosis: 'the ladder is the hypotenuse, so the wall height must be less than 17 ft'; 'longest GIVEN is not the same as hypotenuse -- position relative to the right angle decides'; 'both coordinate differences are legs; PQ itself is the hypotenuse') and for id 4's sketch. Then reconcile the reference material that permitted the omission: amend SKILL.md line 249 so the error-analysis sentence states that the CORRECTION goes through the ordinary types AND the named diagnosis takes a companion manual entry. Enforce with a lint in tests/check_layout.py that fails a problem whose stem contains a diagnosis or construction imperative ('Explain', 'Name the mistake', 'Sketch', 'Draw') and whose id carries no manual entry.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem 1 reads 'Explain why 40 cannot be the hypotenuse, then find the correct one' with a verification JSON holding one approx entry for id 1; assert check_layout.py exits non-zero naming the unflagged diagnosis. It exits 0 today.
improvements.expected_impact: Turns '8 verified, 0 manual' into '8 verified, 5 manual' on a sheet whose instructional_mode is misconception-analysis, where the diagnosis carries most of the credit. Second-largest systemic finding of the run (36 cases); this case and curr-219 are its purest instances.
improvements.risk: Medium. Amending line 249 risks the opposite error -- future error-analysis sheets marking the numeric correction manual too. State the split explicitly: correction checked, diagnosis manual.

improvements.title: Problem 7 records both roots and never records that -56 is rejected
improvements.proposed_change: Support a validity condition on solve entries -- e.g. {"type": "solve", "expr": "x**2 + 33**2 - 65**2", "expected": [56, -56], "admissible": [56], "reject_reason": "a width is a length and cannot be negative"} -- so the checker records both the full solution set and the selection. Have scripts/render_quick_answers.py print the admissible value in the bank (56) rather than the raw list, keeping the rejected root in the detailed solution where the reasoning lives.
improvements.regression_test: Add a verify.py fixture with an admissible subset and assert the entry PASSes only when the key's boxed answer is the admissible value; add a bank case asserting the line reads '56' and not '56, -56'. Today the schema rejects the field and the bank prints both roots.
improvements.expected_impact: A grader marking from the bank stops seeing a rejected root offered as an answer. Applies wherever a physical quantity, a domain restriction or a piece-selection narrows a solution set -- the same class the run's `preserve-domain-restrictions-in-verification` finding covers from the simplification side.
improvements.risk: Medium; a new schema field touches the strict-schema contract whose point is that unknown fields hard-fail, so it needs fixture coverage on both the accept and reject paths.

improvements.title: Problem 4 asks for a sketch; the answer key describes one in prose instead of drawing it
improvements.proposed_change: Have answer_key.tex \input{figure-macros} whenever the worksheet does, and draw problem 4's model response: the segment from A(2,3) to B(7,15) with the horizontal leg of 5 and the vertical leg of 12 labelled and the right angle marked. Enforce generally in tests/check_answer_key.py: when a \problem stem contains a construction imperative ('Sketch', 'Draw', 'Graph'), require the matching solution segment in the key to contain a tikzpicture or a renderer-built figure, and fail otherwise.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair whose worksheet problem 1 says 'Sketch the right triangle' and whose answer key solves it in prose with no tikzpicture; assert check_answer_key.py exits non-zero naming problem 1. Today it passes -- this case is the live instance, with grep 'tikz' answer_key.tex returning 0.
improvements.expected_impact: A student who drew the triangle has nothing to compare against, which is most of the value of a step-by-step key for a construction task. Any sheet using `manual` for a sketch has the same exposure.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. Some construction prompts genuinely have no single model figure (curr-226's 'sketch or describe what the two graphs look like'), so the check should accept an explicitly declared prose-model exemption rather than being absolute.

case_summary: The Pythagorean mathematics is exact -- 10, 12, 15, 13, 41, 10, ±56, 40 -- and the sheet is built around one misconception with unusual discipline: every character's printed wrong answer is that problem's declared trap, and every solution closes with the size check the directions taught ('a leg must come out shorter than the hypotenuse'). The rejection is right on both counts. Four diagnoses (3a, 3b, 5a, 6a) and one required construction (problem 4's sketch) sit inside a sheet declaring zero manual items, on a worksheet whose instructional mode is error analysis, so the responses carrying the focus are the ones outside the trust boundary. And the key genuinely does not draw the sketch it was asked for: answer_key.tex contains no tikz at all and never inputs figure-macros, while worksheet.tex does both. One further defect the judge did not raise: problem 7's Quick Answers line reads '56, -56', offering the rejected root to a grader, because the solve entry records the solution set with no way to record which candidate the context admits.
